images.title: Cut, then count gaps
images.purpose: Show the one idea the student practises: cut each unit into equal gaps, then count gaps from 0 to name a point.
images.composition: One number line across the frame with every gap shown as a soft band, three counting arcs from 0 and one marked point, with wide white space.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 2 with exactly 9 evenly spaced ticks: each unit cut into 4 equal gaps. The 8 gaps are shown as flat bands just under the line, alternating very light teal #0072B2 and plain white. Exactly 3 equal amber #E69F00 arcs above the line, from 0 to the 3rd tick. A reddish purple #CC79A7 point sits on the 3rd tick. Exactly 1 number line, 3 arcs, 1 point.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any on-screen control, panel or app frame drawn around the number line
images.takeaway: Cut the unit into equal gaps, then count the gaps from 0.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into 4 equal gaps; 3 amber arcs count from 0 to a purple point labelled 3/4.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the arcs aloud and say the point's name as 3 gaps of one fourth.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture of cutting and counting gaps primes the practice that follows.
